title: Preeti Pawar, Jasmine Lamboria Reach CWG Boxing Finals as Chopra Eyes Javelin Gold
excerpt: Two Indian boxers booked gold medal bouts on a packed Day 9 in Glasgow, while the mixed 4x400m relay team qualified for Saturday's final and Neeraj Chopra prepares for tonight's javelin showdown against Arshad Nadeem.
body:
• Preeti Pawar swept all five scorecards to beat Zambia's Catherine Mwape 5-0, booking a 54kg boxing final against Canada's Scarlett Delgado on August 1
  • Jasmine Lamboria stopped Lesotho's Maselele by RSC to advance to the women's 57kg final against Northern Ireland's Walsh
  • Neeraj Chopra, Rohit Yadav, and Yashvir Singh will compete in the men's javelin final tonight at 20:15 BST, with rival Arshad Nadeem also in the 12-man field
  • India's mixed 4x400m relay team qualified for Saturday's final with a time of 3:20.98, led by national record holder Vishal TK

India's Commonwealth Games campaign in Glasgow hit full stride on Day 9, with Preeti Pawar and Jasmine Lamboria each reaching their respective boxing finals, the mixed 4x400m relay team booking a spot in Saturday's summit clash, and Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra set to headline the men's javelin final tonight at Hampden Park.

Two Boxing Finalists in a Single Session

Preeti, 21, was ruthless in the women's 54kg semifinal, blanking Zambia's Catherine Mwape 5-0 to extend her perfect Glasgow run to four victories without dropping a single round. The Asian Boxing Championships gold medallist combined precise straight punches with sharp footwork, never allowing Mwape to establish any rhythm.

Her path to the final has been emphatic: a referee-stop-contest win over Malawi's Deborah Mtenje in the round of 16, a 5-0 shutout of Northern Ireland's Nicole Clyde in the quarterfinals, and now an identical scoreline against Mwape. She will face Canada's Scarlett Delgado, who beat England's Lauren Mackie 4-1 in the other semifinal, for gold on Saturday.

"I don't think too much about the medal or the expectations. My focus is to stay disciplined, trust my preparation, and take one bout at a time."

— Preeti Pawar

Jasmine Lamboria joined Preeti in the finals column with a dominant referee-stop-contest victory over Lesotho's Maselele in the women's 57kg semifinal. The Indian, who earlier defeated England's Glynn 4-1 in the quarterfinals, will face Northern Ireland's Walsh for the gold medal on Saturday.

The two finalists are part of India's best-ever CWG boxing campaign. Nine Indian pugilists reached the semifinals in Glasgow, guaranteeing at least as many podium finishes — the largest boxing medal haul by any single nation at these Games.

Chopra vs Nadeem: The Javelin Final

The marquee event of the day arrives tonight, with Neeraj Chopra bidding for his second Commonwealth Games gold eight years after his Gold Coast 2018 triumph. The Olympic champion qualified fifth with a best throw of 79.61m on Thursday, competing in challenging cold and windy conditions that prevented any athlete from hitting the automatic qualifying standard.

"Conditions are not best for javelin throwers. It's not only cold, it's also windy and the wind was not just from the front, sometimes it was from the side. It's really hard to process where we have to throw."

— Neeraj Chopra, after qualifying

All three Indian throwers advanced to the 12-man final: Rohit Yadav (78.37m, 9th) and Yashvir Singh (78.36m, 10th) will compete alongside Chopra. Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem — the Paris 2024 Olympic gold medallist who holds the Games record of 90.18m — also qualified with 78.63m, setting up another chapter of one of athletics' most compelling rivalries.

Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage led qualifiers with 82.84m, while Grenada's Anderson Peters, the Commonwealth record holder, was second at 81.29m. The final is scheduled for 20:15 BST (00:45 IST, August 1).

Relay Team Scrapes Into Final

India's mixed 4x400m relay quartet — Vishal TK, Ansa Babu, Rajesh Ramesh, and Rashdeep Kaur — qualified for Saturday's final with a time of 3:20.98, finishing seventh among the eight finalists. Vishal, who in May became the first Indian man to break the 45-second barrier in the 400m with a national record of 44.98 seconds, anchored the team through the heats.

Nigeria topped the round with 3:14.58, followed by England (3:15.11) and Australia (3:15.21). India will need a significant improvement in Saturday's final at 18:30 BST (23:00 IST) to mount a credible medal challenge.

Diaspora Watch: Glasgow Rallies Behind Team India

With the Games in Glasgow — home to one of the UK's largest South Asian communities — Indian and diaspora fans have been a visible presence at venues across the city. The boxing sessions and athletics events at the SEC and Hampden Park have drawn particularly vocal support, and Saturday's boxing finals and javelin showdown promise packed Indian contingents in the stands.

What's Next

Saturday shapes up as one of the most consequential days for India at Glasgow 2026. Preeti and Jasmine will fight for boxing gold, the relay team will contest the final, and any javelin medals from tonight's final will add to what is already shaping up as India's strongest overall performance at these Games. With the competition entering its final three days, India's contingent is pushing hard for a strong finish across multiple disciplines.
